name: Bedad
overview: Bedad was a male Edomite known for his military leadership, notably defeating the Midianites in the field of Moab. His role as a warrior and leader is recorded in the genealogies of Edom, highlighting his significance among the Edomite chiefs. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Bedad means "solitary," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as recorded in Genesis 36:35. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that may reflect aspects of his character or role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hadad as Bedad's father, as inferred from the genealogical record in Genesis 36:35. Beyond this paternal link, no further family relationships are documented for Bedad.
scriptureSignificance: Bedad holds significance in the biblical narrative as a victorious Edomite chief who led his people in battle against the Midianites in Moab. This military success underscores the strength and influence of Edomite leadership during the period recorded in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. His mention in these genealogies situates him within the broader history of Edom and its interactions with neighboring peoples.
